<!-- Generated by `uv run python -m evals report --task semantic_type --all-items` on 2026-11-20; see planning/jev-and-evals.md for context. -->

> **How to read this.** Full `semantic_type` benchmark: `gpt-5.4-mini`, `jev-1.14.0` and `gpt-5.4` (premium) on 478 chunks from 30 mock postings (written by Claude, labeled by Sonnet and Opus). "agreed" is Opus's label where the two disagree; "adjudicated" is "agreed" with 8 reviewed corrections (section labels and banners that both labelers had labeled by the section they introduce; see `backend/evals/data/labels/adjudications.json`), and is the reference for the detail tables. No pair of models is significantly different on either label set, and the ranking shifts with the label set. `jev-1.14.0` pricing ($0.042 per 1M input tokens) is verified against the TypeSafe console. Run history: `gpt-5.4-mini` and `jev-1.14.0` include 80 repeat calls (`--repeats 2` on 40 items) and `gpt-5.4-mini` had 164 calls retried after Azure rate limiting, so their cost lines include those extra calls.
>
> **Two findings the tables do not show directly** (computed from the saved results). (1) Section labels and banners (the 10 `other` items): `jev-1.14.0` found 8, `gpt-5.4` 4 and `gpt-5.4-mini` 0. (2) All 9 of Jev's errors against the adjudicated labels have confidence below 0.7, so answers at confidence >= 0.7 are 100% accurate on 95.8% of items. Sending the low-confidence answers to `gpt-5.4` instead gives 469/478 (98.1%), the same as Jev alone, at $0.026 against $0.355 for `gpt-5.4` on everything: the fallback fixes about as many answers as it breaks, because the hard items are label-boundary cases. The threshold was chosen on the same data, so treat this as indicative.

# Eval report: semantic_type

478 items. Quality is against each label source separately, on each item's first run; an item whose model gave an invalid answer counts as wrong. Items with no answer because of rate limits or connection errors are excluded, not wrong. Per-class, confusion and calibration tables use the **adjudicated** labels.

## Pairwise (exact McNemar)

- vs agreed labels: gpt-5.4 vs gpt-5.4-mini on 478 items: only gpt-5.4 right on 3, only gpt-5.4-mini right on 4; p = 1.000 (no significant difference)
- vs agreed labels: gpt-5.4 vs jev-1.14.0 on 478 items: only gpt-5.4 right on 11, only jev-1.14.0 right on 4; p = 0.118 (no significant difference)
- vs agreed labels: gpt-5.4-mini vs jev-1.14.0 on 478 items: only gpt-5.4-mini right on 12, only jev-1.14.0 right on 4; p = 0.077 (no significant difference)
- vs adjudicated labels: gpt-5.4 vs gpt-5.4-mini on 478 items: only gpt-5.4 right on 5, only gpt-5.4-mini right on 2; p = 0.453 (no significant difference)
- vs adjudicated labels: gpt-5.4 vs jev-1.14.0 on 478 items: only gpt-5.4 right on 6, only jev-1.14.0 right on 9; p = 0.607 (no significant difference)
- vs adjudicated labels: gpt-5.4-mini vs jev-1.14.0 on 478 items: only gpt-5.4-mini right on 5, only jev-1.14.0 right on 11; p = 0.210 (no significant difference)
